rw1.why: She doubted her equipment because the results clashed with the standard model, so inconsistent is correct. Compatible would give her no reason to doubt.
rw1.passage: The scientist's results were so with the standard model that she spent two years checking her equipment before she dared to publish them.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw1.why: A landmark every sailor knew was prominent. Hidden contradicts that, and the passage does not describe danger or impermanence.
rw1.passage: The old lighthouse, once a landmark that every sailor knew, now stands abandoned, and its beam has not been lit in decades.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw1.why: A village with only wind and a bell is quiet, so the stillness was soothing. Clamour, congestion and bustle describe noise or crowds.
rw1.passage: Tired of the city's constant noise, the poet moved to a village where the only sounds were the wind and the occasional bell, and she found the soothing.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw1.why: Saving a third of the cost implies the expensive item was removed. Defended and doubled would raise the cost, and announced does not explain the saving.
rw1.passage: The board approved the budget only after the director the most expensive item, a decision that saved nearly a third of the cost.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw1.why: The underlined sentence names the addition of pedals as the change that turned a curiosity into transport, which the next sentence confirms with manufacture by the thousand. It does not explain speed or question pedals.
rw1.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original essay about the invention of the bicycle.

The earliest bicycles had no pedals. Riders sat astride a wooden frame and pushed along the ground with their feet, a method that was fast on flat roads but exhausting on hills. It was the addition of pedals to the front wheel, in the 1860s, that turned a curiosity into a means of transport. Within a decade, the machines were being manufactured by the thousand.
rw1.q: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains why the earliest bicycles were fast.
It contrasts bicycles with other methods of transport.
It questions whether pedals were a good idea.
It identifies the change that made the invention practical and popular.

rw1.why: Marit's inability to remember the gate's colour and her sense of waiting suggest disorientation at change. The passage gives no reason for leaving, no clear anger at the owners and is not about the painting.
rw1.passage:
The following text is from an original short story. Marit is visiting the farm where she was raised.

The gate had been painted green since she last saw it, which seemed to Marit an enormous betrayal. She stood with her hand on the new paint and tried to remember what colour it had been, and found she could not. Behind her, the car ticked as it cooled. Somewhere in the house a radio was playing a song she half knew, and she thought that if she waited long enough, someone would come out and tell her what she had forgotten.
rw1.q: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain why Marit left the farm
To show that Marit is angry with the farm's new owners
To convey Marit's disorientation on returning to a place that has changed
To describe the painting of the gate

rw1.why: Text 2 says the studies did not control calories and show only fewer cravings, so they do not show that small meals cut overeating. The dietitian does not endorse or deny cravings entirely, or recommend two meals.
rw1.passage:
Text 1

Some nutrition researchers maintain that eating several small meals a day keeps energy levels steady and prevents overeating. They cite studies in which participants who ate five small meals reported fewer cravings than those who ate two large ones.

Text 2

A dietitian who examined the same studies points out that participants' total calories were not controlled. She argues that the studies show only that people who eat more often report fewer cravings, not that the pattern of meals reduces overeating.
rw1.q: Based on the texts, how would the dietitian in Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that small meals prevent overeating?
choices: By agreeing that small meals prevent overeating in every case
By noting that the studies cited do not show that small meals reduce how much people eat
By recommending that people eat only two meals a day
By arguing that cravings are unrelated to eating habits

rw1.why: The text says frequent buses raise ridership because riders no longer need timetables, and that frequency can matter as much as speed. It does not claim buses are fastest or that timetables are obsolete.
rw1.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original essay about public transport.

Cities that have invested in frequent, reliable buses often find that ridership rises more than planners predicted. Part of the reason is simple: people value not having to check a timetable. When a bus arrives every ten minutes, a rider can leave when ready, and the service becomes something to rely on rather than plan around. Frequency, in other words, can matter as much as speed.
rw1.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Frequent service can attract riders because it makes a bus system easier to rely on.
Buses are faster than any other form of public transport.
Planners rarely predict how many people will use buses.
Timetables are no longer needed in modern cities.

rw1.why: The text rejects the flowing glass idea and offers the glassmaking method instead. It does not say glass flows, call glaziers unskilled, or describe glass as neither solid nor liquid.
rw1.passage:
The following text is from an original essay about glass.

Glass is often described as a slow-moving liquid, and the claim is repeated as evidence in the fact that old window panes are thicker at the bottom. Physicists point out that glass at room temperature is, for all practical purposes, a solid. The uneven panes are better explained by the way medieval glassmakers spun and flattened their molten discs, producing sheets of uneven thickness that glaziers set with the thicker edge down.
rw1.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Glass flows downward at room temperature over centuries.
Medieval glaziers were unskilled and set panes carelessly.
Glass is neither a solid nor a liquid.
A familiar explanation for uneven old window panes is mistaken, and the manufacturing method accounts for them better.

rw1.why: Fastest growth means the biggest proportional increase, and only the first choice reports this for robotics and compares it with others. The others cite single figures or other clubs.
rw1.passage: A school recorded the number of students who joined each after-school club this year. The head teacher wants to emphasise that the robotics club grew fastest.
rw1.q: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: Membership of the robotics club rose from 18 students to 41, and the drama club had 52 members.
Membership of the chess club rose from 30 to 36 students, the smallest increase.
Membership of the robotics club more than doubled, from 18 students to 41, a larger proportional increase than in either the chess or the drama club.
Membership of the drama club was higher than that of the robotics club in both years.

rw1.why: The claim is of a quick initial rise and slower later growth, which the first choice reports using the graph. The others describe a fall, steady growth, or only the final value.
rw1.passage: A researcher measured the average daily number of steps taken by workers at a company during a six-week programme that offered prizes for activity. She wants to claim that participation raised steps most in the first weeks.

choices: average daily steps fell from 8,000 in week 2 to 5,000 in week 6.
average daily steps rose steadily by 500 each week from week 0 to week 6.
average daily steps were 9,000 in week 6, the highest of the programme.
average daily steps rose from 5,000 in week 0 to 8,000 in week 2, but then rose by only 1,000 more over the next four weeks.

rw1.why: The claim links her writing to her view, and the quotation describing short essays about single decisions shows her method matching her view that ethics is learned through cases. The others describe her attitude, an example, or her contemporaries.
rw1.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original essay about a philosopher.

The philosopher Edith Clarion was suspicious of grand systems. Where her contemporaries sought a single principle that would explain all of ethics, she wrote short, particular essays about a single decision: whether to tell a friend a painful truth, or how to divide an inheritance fairly. Ethics, she argued, is learned through cases, not derived from theory.
rw1.q: A student claims that Clarion's method of writing reflected her philosophical view. Which quotation from the text best supports the student's claim?
choices: "she wrote short, particular essays about a single decision"
"The philosopher Edith Clarion was suspicious of grand systems."
"whether to tell a friend a painful truth"
"Where her contemporaries sought a single principle that would explain all of ethics"

rw1.why: Faster sleep in the cooler room is the direct support for the claim. The other choices describe the design without the result.
rw1.passage:
A researcher claims that sleeping in a cooler room helps people fall asleep more quickly.

In a laboratory study, volunteers slept on different nights in a room kept at 16 degrees Celsius and in a room kept at 24 degrees. On average, volunteers fell asleep nine minutes faster in the cooler room than in the warmer one.
rw1.q: Which finding from the text most directly supports the researcher's claim?
choices: The volunteers slept in the laboratory on different nights.
Volunteers fell asleep an average of nine minutes sooner in the cooler room.
One room was kept at 24 degrees Celsius.
The study involved both a cooler and a warmer room.

rw1.why: Seedlings with varying temperature grew taller and thicker, so moderate variation may stimulate growth. The other choices contradict the result or go beyond it.
rw1.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original science article.

Researchers placed identical seedlings in two greenhouses. One greenhouse was kept at a constant temperature, and the other varied by five degrees over each day. The seedlings in the varying greenhouse grew taller and developed thicker stems. This suggests that moderate daily changes in temperature
rw1.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: always harm the growth of seedlings.
have no effect on how plants develop.
may stimulate growth in these seedlings.
are less important than the amount of water.

rw1.why: Visitors lingered when labels asked questions, so the curator likely thinks questions prompt closer looking. The text does not say visitors dislike labels or that facts are useless.
rw1.passage:
The following text is from an original essay about museums.

Visitors to a museum often spend longer in front of a single work when a label asks a question about it than when the label simply states facts. A curator who noticed this pattern has begun to revise the museum's labels. It seems likely that the curator believes that
rw1.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: questions encourage visitors to look more closely at a work.
facts are of no use to museum visitors.
works of art should have no labels.

rw1.why: Last summer calls for the simple past tense, discovered. The other forms do not fit the time frame.
rw1.passage: The botanist the rare orchid in a remote part of the mountains last summer.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: The subject decision is singular, and the phrase beginning with along with does not make it plural, so was agrees.
rw1.passage: The decision to close the school, along with the plans for relocating the pupils, announced on Monday.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: Two independent clauses are joined with a semicolon. A comma alone would create a comma splice.
rw1.passage: The city has several fine parks the largest, Riverside Park, covers two hundred acres.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: The comparison is completed by the clause than I am, so the subject pronoun I is correct.
rw1.passage: Lena is a better swimmer than .
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: An adverb is needed to modify the verb conducted, so carefully is correct.
rw1.passage: The scientists conducted the experiment and recorded the results in a notebook.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: The possessive relative pronoun whose connects to the discoveries. Who's means who is.
rw1.passage: Marie Curie, discoveries transformed physics and chemistry, won two Nobel Prizes.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

rw1.why: The final plan differs from the first draft, so However is the logical transition.
rw1.passage: The first draft of the plan called for a single large library. the final plan includes three smaller branches closer to residents.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

rw1.why: The sentence contrasts the well-studied honeybee with the poorly known solitary bees, so By contrast is correct.
rw1.passage: Few insects are as well studied as the honeybee. the habits of many solitary bees remain largely unknown.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

rw1.why: The studies cast doubt on the mayor's promise, so Yet is the logical transition.
rw1.passage: The mayor promised to reduce traffic by building a new road. studies suggest that new roads often attract more cars than they remove.
rw1.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

rw1.why: Speed is shown by the short time between the start of construction and opening, which the first choice states. The others give size, a start date or the reason for the bridge.
rw1.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Calder Footbridge crosses the River Wend in the north of England.
  • It is 85 metres long.
  • It replaced an older bridge washed away by floods.
  • Construction began in March 2022.
  • The bridge opened to the public only eleven weeks later.

The student wants to emphasise the unusual speed of a project.
rw1.q: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Calder Footbridge, which replaced an older bridge washed away by floods, opened only eleven weeks after construction began.
The Calder Footbridge, which crosses the River Wend, is 85 metres long.
Construction of the Calder Footbridge began in March 2022.
The Calder Footbridge replaced an older bridge that had been washed away.

rw1.why: To introduce the writer, the choice must name her, say what she writes and indicate her standing, which the first choice does.
rw1.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Nadia Solberg is a Norwegian novelist.
  • Her first novel, The Quiet Fjord, appeared in 2014.
  • Her books are set in small coastal communities.
  • She has won two national literary prizes.
  • Her work has been translated into fourteen languages.

The student wants to introduce a writer to someone who has not read her work.
rw1.q: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Her work has been translated into fourteen languages.
The Quiet Fjord was her first novel and appeared in 2014.
Nadia Solberg, a Norwegian novelist whose books are set in small coastal communities, has won two national literary prizes.
A novelist with two prizes has been widely translated.

rw1.why: To explain a cause, the choice needs both the reason and the effect, which the first choice provides. The others state a fact or only the effect.
rw1.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Many tropical rainforest soils are low in nutrients.
  • Most nutrients are stored in living plants rather than in the soil.
  • When forests are cleared, the nutrients are lost.
  • After clearing, farmland in these areas often becomes unproductive within a few years.
  • Rainforests cover about six percent of Earth's land surface.

The student wants to explain a cause.
rw1.q: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Rainforests cover about six percent of Earth's land surface.
Many tropical rainforest soils are low in nutrients.
Because most nutrients in rainforest soils are stored in plants rather than in the ground, clearing the forest removes them, which is why farmland there often becomes unproductive within a few years.
Farmland in cleared rainforest areas often becomes unproductive within a few years.

rw2h.why: She neither flatters nor condemns and leaves the verdict to readers, which makes her tone dispassionate. Effusive and sentimental imply warmth, and accusatory implies condemnation.
rw2h.passage: The biographer's tone is notably : she neither flatters her subject nor condemns him, setting out his decisions and their consequences and leaving readers to reach their own verdict.
rw2h.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw2h.why: An alliance that dissolved as soon as the common rival was beaten was weak, which tenuous means. Durable contradicts the dissolution.
rw2h.passage: Theirs was a alliance, formed less from shared goals than from a common rival, and it dissolved the moment the rival was defeated.
rw2h.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw2h.why: Ostensibly marks the stated purpose, and the contrast is with the real, underlying purpose. Stated would repeat the surface meaning, and the purpose was not accidental.
rw2h.passage: While the senator's speech was ostensibly a defence of free trade, its purpose, critics argued, was to reassure donors who owned factories abroad.
rw2h.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw2h.why: Remarks that let everyone hear what they already believed must have been open to many readings, so ambiguous fits. Blunt would be direct, and the others do not explain the effect.
rw2h.passage: The politician's remarks were intentionally , so that listeners of all persuasions could hear in them something they already believed.
rw2h.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

rw2h.why: The underlined sentence concedes that the method was tedious and used a single subject but says it still gave the first quantitative description of forgetting. It does not dismiss the work, explain syllable choice, or criticise later researchers.
rw2h.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original essay about the study of memory.

In the 1880s, the psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus set out to measure memory by memorising lists of nonsense syllables, reasoning that meaningless items would be free of prior associations. His method was tedious and his only subject was himself, yet it produced the first quantitative description of forgetting. Later researchers would refine his curves, but the basic pattern he found, a steep early loss followed by a gentle decline, has held up.
rw2h.q: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It dismisses Ebbinghaus's work as unscientific.
It explains why Ebbinghaus chose nonsense syllables.
It argues that later researchers misread Ebbinghaus's curves.
It acknowledges the limits of a method while stressing the importance of its results.

rw2h.why: The final sentence uses the statue facing the wrong way as an image for a story that credits the wrong person. It says nothing of when the statue was made or of destroying the letter, and the explanation of the land comes earlier.
rw2h.passage:
The following text is from an original novel. Beatrix, a young archivist, has found a letter that contradicts a famous story about her city's founding.

Beatrix read the letter a third time, as though the words might rearrange themselves. The founder had not, as every schoolchild knew, bought the land; he had been given it, and by a woman whose name appeared nowhere in the textbooks. She thought of the statue in the square, the founder's hand extended in what she had always taken for generosity. It occurred to her that the statue was not wrong, exactly; it had simply been turned to face the wrong way.
rw2h.q: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It reveals that the statue was erected after the letter was written.
It uses an image to suggest that a familiar story misrepresents who deserves credit.
It shows that Beatrix intends to destroy the letter.
It explains how the founder obtained the land.

rw2h.why: Text 2 says earlier hand-copied pamphlets failed to spread and that political support mattered, so the claim overstates the press. The scholar does not deny printing or say earlier reformers avoided pamphlets.
rw2h.passage:
Text 1

Some historians argue that the printing press made the Reformation possible: without cheap, rapidly produced pamphlets, they say, Luther's ideas could not have reached so many people so quickly.

Text 2

A scholar of religious history notes that earlier reform movements also produced pamphlets, copied by hand, and that many failed to spread beyond their regions. She suggests that Luther's success owed as much to the political support of local rulers as to the press.
rw2h.q: Based on the texts, how would the scholar in Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?
choices: By denying that Luther's pamphlets were ever printed
By arguing that the claim gives too little weight to factors other than printing
By agreeing that printing alone explains the Reformation
By saying that earlier reformers made no use of pamphlets

rw2h.why: The text says the retreat was plain but the main finding was the faster flow. Satellite photographs are not said to be the only method, the glacier retreated, and meltwater is said to lubricate the bed.
rw2h.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original science article.

When the satellite photographs of the glacier were compared with those taken thirty years earlier, the retreat was plain: the ice front had withdrawn by almost two kilometres. But the glaciologists' main finding concerned the speed of the ice rather than its length. The flow near the front had accelerated, apparently because meltwater was lubricating the bed, and the faster flow was moving ice toward the sea more quickly than the older models had allowed.
rw2h.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The glaciologists found that the glacier's acceleration, more than its retreat, shows that ice is reaching the sea faster than earlier models allowed.
Satellite photographs are the only reliable way to measure a glacier's length.
The glacier has advanced by almost two kilometres in thirty years.
Meltwater cannot affect the speed at which a glacier flows.

rw2h.why: The text contrasts the earlier honour given to copying with the modern idea of originality. It does not say apprentices were forbidden individual styles, that modern painters never copy, or that copying was considered theft.
rw2h.passage:
The following text is from an original essay about copying in art.

In the history of European painting, copying was long regarded as an honourable discipline, not a form of theft. Apprentices spent years reproducing the works of masters, and a painter who could convincingly imitate an earlier style was praised. The modern prejudice that originality means starting from nothing would have puzzled such artists, who thought of invention as the skilful reworking of what the tradition already offered.
rw2h.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Apprentices were forbidden from developing their own styles.
Modern painters never copy the works of earlier masters.
Copying was once considered a form of theft by painters.
Earlier painters valued imitation and reworking of tradition as part of invention, unlike the modern view of originality.

rw2h.why: A pronounced wet season means a large seasonal swing, which the first choice shows for Altamar compared with the small variation in Brevik. The others describe only Brevik, one month, or a trend common to both.
rw2h.passage: A researcher compared the average monthly rainfall in two cities, Altamar and Brevik, over a year. A student wants to claim that Altamar has a more pronounced wet season.
rw2h.q: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the student's claim?
choices: Rainfall in Brevik peaks at 100 millimetres in July and falls to 70 in January.
Rainfall in Altamar in January is 50 millimetres, lower than in Brevik.
Rainfall in Altamar peaks at 190 millimetres in July, almost four times its January level of 50, while Brevik's rainfall varies only between 70 and 100.
Rainfall in both cities is higher in July than in January.
